headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if MinerU parses Kestra-produced files or messages as trusted content; data leakage is moderate due to shared file/API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write files, emit messages/notifications, and use stdin/stdout; MinerU ingests local documents and exposes an MCP server. If Kestra-generated content is fed into MinerU, raw content could be misread as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are copied into MinerU inputs without provenance tagging
IF MinerU MCP tools accept untrusted document text as instructions
mitigations: Tag Kestra outputs as data-only before ingestion
Disable MCP access for untrusted document sources
Separate workflow output folders from MinerU input folders
Add a manual review step before MinerU processes Kestra artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, OCR text, and other document content. A shared workspace or handoff can expose sensitive documents to both agents; MinerU is documented as offline, but Kestra has broad network egress, so leakage risk is real though not automatically uncontrolled.
conditions: IF Kestra writes sensitive artifacts into a directory MinerU can read
IF MinerU processes documents containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Restrict Kestra output directories to non-sensitive paths
Run MinerU on a separate copy of inputs
Redact secrets before orchestration handoff
Disable unnecessary Kestra notifications for sensitive jobs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress; MinerU uses MCP and concurrent inference. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared MCP-backed resources, concurrent writes or conflicting actions can corrupt state. Kestra's elevated privilege request increases blast radius, while MinerU's concurrency adds contention risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or shared resource
IF Kestra workflows and MinerU sessions run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable shared MCP resources for concurrent jobs
Run one agent at a time for mutable targets
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow artifacts and notifications that MinerU may later consume as documents. If MinerU treats those outputs as authoritative extracted text, errors or injected content can cascade into downstream processing. The pair does not document a verification boundary, so the risk exists in default handoff patterns but is not guaranteed.
conditions: IF MinerU consumes Kestra-produced artifacts without validation
IF downstream automation acts on MinerU output as final truth
mitigations: Require checksum or schema validation between agents
Add human review for high-impact outputs
Keep Kestra as producer and MinerU as read-only parser
Annotate provenance on every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database, cloud storage, messages, and notifications, while MinerU processes document formats and is described as fully offline. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to gaps in how the operator routes regulated data between them. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Kestra into MinerU without policy review
IF notifications or logs include restricted document contents
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from test runs
Review retention settings for Kestra logs and artifacts
Keep MinerU offline for sensitive documents
Document data-class handling for each workflow
